Important

Requires Termux. Do NOT use the Google Play version (outdated and abandoned); get it from F-Droid or GitHub Releases.

In Termux, paste this to download VibraVid, compile the components (including Velora) and set up the storage folder:

curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManoloZocco/StreamingCommunity/main/termux_install.sh | bash

Then launch it any time with vibravid.

See also: Login guide, NAS deployment.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
At interactive CLI startup VibraVid checks GitHub Releases in the background (cached 24 h) and prints the command for your installation if a newer release exists. VibraVid --check-update checks on demand; --skip-update-check disables the startup check (auto_check_update = false in config.toml for good).

Installation Update Binary (Windows / macOS / Linux) VibraVid -UP Docker docker compose pull && docker compose up -d Manual clone git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main, then sync dependencies (table above)

Folders ignored by .gitignore (e.g. Video/) are not deleted by the reset. If the folder isn't a git repository yet:

git init
git remote add origin https://github.com/AstraeLabs/VibraVid.git
git fetch origin
git reset --hard origin/main

docs.title: Custom multi-source downloads
docs.text:
Generic_Downloader downloads every selected track from every source in sources concurrently on one progress bar and muxes them into one file, including hybrid Dolby Vision + HDR10 (the DV RPU is injected into the HDR10 base via mkvmerge/dovi_tool).

Full manifests (DASH MPD, HLS master) are auto-selected by codec/resolution/range, including the DV base/companion pairing with custom_filters={"video": "hybrid"} (see Companion Dolby Vision), across any number of sources and without per-source tagging.

from VibraVid.core.downloader import Generic_Downloader

sources = [
    {"url": "<hdr10+dv m3u8>", "key": "<kid:key>"},
    {"role": "audio", "language": "en", "url": "<audio m3u8>", "key": "<kid:key>"},
    {"role": "subtitle", "language": "en", "url": "<sub url>"},
]

Generic_Downloader(
    sources=sources,
    output_path="./Video/out.mkv",
    custom_filters={"video": "hybrid"},
).start()
  • role: video, audio, subtitle (a range tag like video:hdr10 is only a label). Needed only for attribute-less rendition manifests (e.g. Apple TV+) to tell sources apart.
  • Optional per-source fields: language, name, label, headers, cookies, protocol.
  • Test runs: max_segments=N or max_time="HH:MM:SS"; a clip: max_segments="10-50" or max_time="00:01:00-00:05:00".

docs.title: Directory layout
docs.text:
VibraVid/services/<name>/
├── __init__.py     # CLI entry point: search(), title_search(), --url resolution
├── client.py       # auth + low-level HTTP
├── scrapper.py     # metadata (title/season/episode info)
└── downloader.py   # builds DASH_Downloader / HLS_Downloader and starts it

The split isn't enforced: only __init__.py with a search() function is required.

docs.title: Registration (auto-discovery)
docs.text:
VibraVid/services/_base/site_loader.py scans VibraVid/services/*/__init__.py at startup. Two module-level names are required:

indice = 900            # position in the CLI/GUI site list; pick a free number, the loader renumbers on the next run
_useFor = "Film_Serie"  # Anime, Film_Serie, Serie, Song or Tor

To keep a service out of the CLI, TUI and GUI while you build it, list its folder name in hidden_services (configuration); it is not loaded at all until you remove it.

The folder name must be a valid Python identifier if any code references it with a literal import (from VibraVid.services.<name>.scrapper import X). The loader itself works with any name; for other names resolve submodules dynamically with resolve_service_submodule(module_name, submodule) (VibraVid/services/_base/site_loader.py), see the GUI adapter below.

docs.title: Loading services from a remote repository
docs.text: An imp_service entry can be a GitHub/Gitea repository URL laid out like VibraVid/services/ (one subfolder per service, each __init__.py defining indice/_useFor). Private repos, #ref pinning and caching: see imp_service.

docs.title: CLI options (--url, etc.)
docs.text:
Expose register_cli_args(parser) -> list[str]; the CLI adds the flags and stores their values in context_tracker.site_options, keyed by argparse dest:

def register_cli_args(parser) -> list:
    group = parser.add_argument_group("MyService options (-i <n>)")
    group.add_argument("--url", dest="url", default=None, help="Direct title URL.")
    return ["url"]

Read it in search():

def search(string_to_search=None, get_onlyDatabase=False, direct_item=None, selections=None, scrape_serie=None):
    if direct_item is None and not get_onlyDatabase:
        url = (context_tracker.site_options or {}).get("url")
        if url:
            direct_item = _resolve_url_to_item(url)
    return base_search(..., direct_item=direct_item, ...)

Users can set a default for these options with args = "--url ..." in the service's login.toml section (details). Nothing to do in the service: context_tracker.site_options already contains them, and a command-line flag wins.

base_search / base_process_search_result (VibraVid/services/_base/site_search_manager.py) handle season/episode selection, the results table and dispatch to your download_film / download_series. Reuse them.

docs.title: Authentication (client.py)
docs.text:
No fixed pattern (credential logins, static tokens, session cookies, sometimes several per site). What generalizes:

  • Cache the session on disk if login is costly (rate limits, multi-step handshake): VibraVid.utils.disk_cache (load/save/is_fresh), keyed by service name, with an expiry timestamp. Otherwise every CLI run re-authenticates and backends may throttle or block.
  • A fresh HTTP client per request drops cookies from earlier responses. Capture the session cookie after login (dict(http_client.cookies)) and pass cookies=... to every later create_client(...).
  • A "web session" and an "app/API session" can be unrelated logins on the same domain. If an endpoint returns empty/short data despite a valid session, check whether it belongs to a different auth path.
  • For IP/region use VibraVid.utils.http_client.get_my_location() (cached in .cache/ip.json).

docs.title: Metadata (scrapper.py)
docs.text:
Fill VibraVid.services._base.object.Episode/Season (CLI) or the GUI's Entries/Episode/Season dataclasses (GUI/searchapp/api/base.py) with everything the site gives you:

  • image on search results and episodes: the GUI hero background and episode thumbnails fall back to Entries.poster/Episode.image; empty is a visible regression.
  • slug must be a human-readable title slug, never an opaque content ID: TMDB year/poster lookups use it as the search key and silently miss otherwise.
  • Prefer the site's own release year over a TMDB guess; the TMDB slug/name lookup is only a fallback.
  • If the year is unknown, use the string "9999": EntriesManager.add() treats it as the trigger for the TMDB year lookup (current year if no key or no match). An empty year skips the fallback (VibraVid/services/_base/object.py).
  • TV/series services: add the module name to _TV_MATCH_SITES in VibraVid/services/_base/tmdb_artwork.py. Series/episode TMDB matching (artwork, season names) is gated by it; without it resolve_series_tmdb_id() returns None even with a key. Movies have no allowlist.

docs.title: Building the download (downloader.py)
docs.text:
• If a license/session token is available before the manifest is parsed, pass license_url + license_headers to DASH_Downloader/HLS_Downloader instead of a license_request_fn callback. The CDM pipeline (VibraVid/core/drm/widevine.py / playready.py) already POSTs with your headers; use a callback only when the request needs per-challenge server-side computation.
  • Always pass a non-empty license_url, even when a callback does the request. The vault stores keys by license_url; None/empty makes the save fail with HTTP 400 and the key is lost for reuse (the download still succeeds).
  • If DRM scheme limits quality (one scheme tops out below the other), choose drm_preference from the user's target quality instead of hardcoding.

Non-standard license flows, forced tracks, chapters, status line, custom manifests and music services: Advanced / optional features.

docs.title: GUI adapter
docs.text:
Add GUI/searchapp/api/<name>.py subclassing GenericStreamingAPI (GUI/searchapp/api/generic.py):

from VibraVid.services.<name>.scrapper import GetSerieInfo
from .base import Entries
from .generic import GenericStreamingAPI

class MyService(GenericStreamingAPI):
    site_name = "<name>"
    log_label = "MyService"

    def _build_scraper(self, media_item: Entries):
        return GetSerieInfo(media_item.id)

Auto-discovered like the CLI module (GUI/searchapp/api/__init__.py scans the package); no registration and no logo asset needed. search() and get_series_metadata() already call your CLI-side search()/scrapper; override _build_entry/_map_episode only if the default mapping doesn't fit.

If <name> isn't a valid identifier, resolve the submodule dynamically (see GUI/searchapp/api/appletv.py):

from VibraVid.services._base.site_loader import resolve_service_submodule

class MyService(GenericStreamingAPI):
    site_name = "3dservice"

    def _build_scraper(self, media_item: Entries):
        scrapper = resolve_service_submodule("3dservice", "scrapper")
        return scrapper.GetSerieInfo(media_item.id)

To pin a position in the GUI site list instead of being appended, add the module name to _PREFERRED_ORDER in GUI/searchapp/api/__init__.py (cosmetic only). The category comes from _useFor.

docs.title: License/DRM patterns
docs.text:
Beyond the base license_url / license_headers / license_request_fn case (Building the download):

Dynamic query string. Bake computed params into license_url instead of license_headers:

license_url = (
    f"https://license.example.com/widevine"
    f"?AccountId={account_id}&ContentId={content_id}&SubContentType=Default"
)
dl = DASH_Downloader(mpd_url, license_url=license_url, license_headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})

Multiple outputs. When the license needs URL, params and headers together, return a tuple and unpack it in downloader.py:

def generate_license_url(tracking_info: dict) -> tuple[str, dict, dict]:
    license_url = f"https://license.example.com/{tracking_info['asset_id']}"
    license_params = {"sessionId": tracking_info["session_id"]}
    license_headers = {"X-Auth-Token": tracking_info["token"]}
    return license_url, license_params, license_headers

license_url, license_params, license_headers = generate_license_url(tracking_info)
if license_params:
    license_url += "?" + urlencode(license_params)
dl = DASH_Downloader(mpd_url, license_url=license_url, license_headers=license_headers)

Stateful exchange. For a lease that must be renewed/retried, pass a closure as license_request_fn:

def _make_license_request_fn(asset_id: str, session_token: str):
    def _request(challenge: bytes, headers: dict) -> bytes:
        resp = client.post(
            f"https://license.example.com/lease/{asset_id}",
            content=challenge,
            headers={**headers, "X-Session-Token": session_token},
        )
        resp.raise_for_status()
        return resp.content
    return _request

dl = DASH_Downloader(
    mpd_url,
    license_url=f"https://license.example.com/lease/{asset_id}",  # still required
    license_request_fn=_make_license_request_fn(asset_id, session_token),
)

Direct DRM manager access. Last resort, only if you must resolve keys outside the downloader's DRM flow:

keys = dl.drm_manager.get_wv_keys(pssh, license_url, license_certificate, headers, key=None)

Which CDM the service will use. The user picks it with cdm (Configuration); never open a .wvd / .prd yourself. To know what you're dealing with (e.g. Chrome vs Android identity), ask the core:

from VibraVid.setup import resolve_service_cdm_info

widevine = resolve_service_cdm_info("myservice", height=1080).get("widevine")
# None                       -> no Widevine CDM
# {"remote": False, "path", "type": "CHROME" | "ANDROID", "security_level", ...}   local .wvd
# {"remote": True, "name", "type": "CHROME" | "ANDROID", "security_level"}         remote CDM
# {"path", "error"}          -> the .wvd could not be read

height is the quality you are about to request; it selects the min_height / max_height rule.

docs.title: Custom filter override
docs.text:
To force a track (e.g. an audio language) beyond the config filters, set custom_filters on the downloader instead of adding a constructor argument:

dl = DASH_Downloader(...)
dl.custom_filters = {"audio": config_manager.config.get("DOWNLOAD", "select_audio")}
dl.start()

docs.title: Custom ad-skip (ad_decision_fn)
docs.text:
For sites that stitch ads (SSAI bumpers/creatives) into the manifest, keep the ad knowledge in the service. DASH_Downloader / HLS_Downloader / ISM_Downloader take a decision callback as ad_decision_fn; the pipeline applies it symmetrically to video and audio (no desync), and "keep everything" is the answer on any doubt:

# VibraVid/services/<name>/ads.py (stdlib only, no core imports, unit-testable)
def my_ad_decision(manifest_kind: str, content: str | None, ctx: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    if manifest_kind == "dash":
        ...  # parse the MPD, find ad Periods
        return {"drop_period_idx": [1, 3], "reason": "video-only bumpers"}
    if manifest_kind == "hls":
        ...  # parse the child playlist, find ad ranges/blocks
        return {"drop_seg_idx": [133, 134], "keep_init_urls": ["https://cdn.../init-main.mp4"]}
    if manifest_kind == "ism":
        ...  # scan StreamIndex Name/Url for creative markers
        return {"drop_url_substrings": ["preroll"]}
    return {}

Decision shapes (all optional; {} keeps everything):

  • DASH: {"drop_period_idx": [...], "reason": str}, dropped from every stream; same-language audio continuations split across periods are rejoined.
  • HLS: {"keep_init_urls": [...]} (MAP-block level) and/or {"drop_seg_idx": [...]} (playlist-order indices, per rendition).
  • ISM: {"drop_url_substrings": [...]} (matched against segment URLs) and/or {"drop_seg_idx": [...]} (timeline indices).

Pass it only on the stitched path:

from .ads import my_ad_decision

dl = DASH_Downloader(mpd_url, ..., ad_decision_fn=my_ad_decision)
dl.start()

docs.title: Batch downloads (albums, season packs)
docs.text:
So one failed item doesn't abort the batch, catch per-item errors and report them with context_tracker.report_download_error(message) / report_download_success() (VibraVid/core/ui/tracker.py); GUI/CLI then show a partial-success summary:

from VibraVid.core.ui.tracker import context_tracker

for item in items_to_download:
    try:
        download_track(item)
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.error(f"Track '{item.name}' failed: {exc}")
        context_tracker.report_download_error(f"{item.name}: {exc}")
        continue
    context_tracker.report_download_success()

docs.title: Chapters
docs.text:
Pass chapter markers as chapters= to DASH_Downloader / HLS_Downloader; each is {"name": str, "seconds": int}.

Known up front:

chapters = [
    {"name": "Intro", "seconds": 0},
    {"name": "Main content", "seconds": 45},
    {"name": "Credits", "seconds": 1620},
]
dl = DASH_Downloader(mpd_url, chapters=chapters or None)

Arriving during a live/long download: pass one mutable list and keep appending to that same object from a background thread; the downloader reads it once, at final mux time.

chapters: list = []
dl = DASH_Downloader(mpd_url, chapters=chapters)
threading.Thread(target=_watch_and_append, args=(chapters, record_start), daemon=True).start()
dl.start()

def _watch_and_append(chapters: list, record_start: float) -> None:
    last_seen = None
    while not stop_flag.wait(POLL_INTERVAL):
        marker = poll_current_marker()
        if marker and marker != last_seen:
            last_seen = marker
            chapters.append({"name": marker, "seconds": int(time.time() - record_start)})

docs.title: Live status line (long-running/live downloads)
docs.text:
To show a changing status above the progress bars (connection state, a counter), use the shared status line instead of printing lines that scroll past the bars:

from VibraVid.core.ui.bar_manager import get_bar_manager

bar_manager = get_bar_manager(download_id)
if bar_manager:
    bar_manager.set_status_text("[cyan]your rich-markup status text")

Call it whenever the state changes (no built-in polling). The text is also logged as [msg_room], so don't add your own logger.info for it.

docs.title: Custom manifest format
docs.text:
If the site has no standard DASH/HLS manifest, don't write a bespoke downloader: build a vibravid_manifest from the resolved tracks (format: Custom JSON manifest; parser: VibraVid/core/manifest/custom.py) and hand it to the existing downloaders:

manifest = {"vibravid_manifest": True, "base_url": "https://cdn.example.com/movie/", "duration": 5400, "tracks": [...]}
dl = DASH_Downloader(json.dumps(manifest))

docs.title: Search backed by TMDB
docs.text:
If the site has no usable search (or too sparse to build listings and season/episode structure), use TMDB as the search backend. It needs a TMDB API key; without one the service returns zero results silently, so don't use it as a hidden fallback.

from VibraVid.provider.tmdb import tmdb

def search(query: str) -> list[Entries]:
    results = []
    for movie in tmdb.search_movies(query):
        results.append(Entries(
            id=movie["id"], name=movie["title"], slug=movie["title"],
            type="movie", year=movie.get("release_date", "")[:4],
            image=f"https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/w500{movie.get('poster_path')}" if movie.get("poster_path") else None,
        ))
    for show in tmdb.search_series(query):
        results.append(Entries(id=show["id"], name=show["name"], slug=show["name"],
                               type="tv", year=show.get("first_air_date", "")[:4]))
    return results

For series, build seasons/episodes in GetSerieInfo from tmdb._make_request(f"tv/{id}") and tv/{id}/season/{n}. Resolving a chosen result to a playable item/URL on the site stays site-specific.

docs.title: Music services (lyrics & tagging)
docs.text:
For audio-only services the final step is VibraVid.core.muxing.helper.audio.process_song(...), not video muxing.

  • Lyrics: VibraVid.provider.musiclyric.get_lyrics(title, artist, album, duration_seconds) has a multi-provider fallback chain and converts synced TTML lyrics to LRC.
  • Tagging: pass track_number, cover_url, album_artist and lyrics to process_song(...) when the site exposes them.
lyrics_result = None
try:
    lyrics_result = get_lyrics(title=title, artist=artist, album=album, duration_seconds=duration)
except Exception:
    logger.error(f"lyrics lookup crashed for {title!r}")

final_path = process_song(
    file_path=downloaded_path,
    title=title,
    artist=artist,
    album=album,
    track_number=track_number,
    cover_url=cover_url,
    album_artist=album_artist,
    lyrics=(lyrics_result or {}).get("lyrics"),
)

TMDB poster/still embedding is separate and automatic once image/slug/year are filled per Metadata.

Users can install and remove your service from the GUI: see Custom service upload.

docs.title: ARR Integration
docs.text:
The ARR block enables VibraVid to work as an automation layer between Seerr/Jellyseerr, Sonarr, Radarr, and the final media library. When enabled, VibraVid polls Sonarr/Radarr for missing media, receives webhook events, downloads through its provider pipeline, and reports the resulting files back so that Sonarr/Radarr can import them.

Important

The ARR integration requires the VibraVid web GUI to be running. All polling loops, webhook listeners, and download workers are managed by the Django application server. The CLI (vibraNid / python -m VibraVid) does not start the ARR stack.

Typical flow:

Seerr / Jellyseerr
    ↓ user requests a movie or series
Sonarr / Radarr
    ↓ media is added and marked as missing
VibraVid ARR
    ↓ detects missing media through polling or webhooks
VibraVid downloader
    ↓ searches and downloads through the configured provider or through the provider selected by tag
Sonarr / Radarr
    ↓ rescans/imports the downloaded file
Media library
    ↓ Jellyfin/Plex can detect the final file

docs.title: Supported integrations
docs.text: Service Role Seerr/Jellyseerr Handles user requests and sends approval/pending webhook events Sonarr Manages TV series, missing episodes, episode metadata, rescans and imports Radarr Manages movies, missing movie metadata, rescans and imports VibraVid Searches, downloads and hands files back to Sonarr/Radarr

ENABLE_SONARR_WEBHOOK=true            # enable_sonarr_webhook
ENABLE_RADARR_WEBHOOK=true            # enable_radarr_webhook

Each of these mirrors the identically-named ARR.* key in config.toml (comment shows the matching key) — set either the env var or the config key, not both.

Tip

Strict TMDB/TVDB identity matching (used when resolving Sonarr/Radarr items) requires a TMDB API key — see TMDB API Key for setup.

docs.title: Webhook setup
docs.text:
VibraVid exposes one webhook endpoint per ARR application. Add one connection only per app — adding multiple webhooks for the same app causes duplicate processing.

When the GUI/Django server is running, the ARR integration exposes dedicated webhook endpoints:

POST /api/arr/webhook/seerr/
POST /api/arr/webhook/sonarr/
POST /api/arr/webhook/radarr/

Each endpoint can be protected with its own webhook secret. Configure the same secret both in VibraVid and in the corresponding external service.

Radarr -> Settings -> Connect -> Webhook

Field Value URL http://<vibravid-host>:<port>/api/arr/webhook/radarr/ Triggers On Movie Added, On Movie File Delete Secret any value mirrored in radarr_webhook.webhook_secret

Sonarr -> Settings -> Connect -> Webhook

Field Value URL http://<vibravid-host>:<port>/api/arr/webhook/sonarr/ Triggers On Series Add, On Episode File Delete Secret any value mirrored in sonarr_webhook.webhook_secret

Then enable in config.toml: 

enable_sonarr_webhook = true
enable_radarr_webhook = true

Note

Webhooks and polling can be used together: webhooks trigger an immediate download when media is added, polling acts as a safety net for items that arrive without a webhook event.

docs.title: Manual and automatic sync
docs.text:
ARR can process media in two ways:

  1. Polling — VibraVid periodically asks Sonarr/Radarr for wanted or missing media.
  2. Webhooks — VibraVid reacts immediately when Seerr, Sonarr or Radarr sends an event.

Both modes can be enabled together. Native Sonarr/Radarr webhooks can be prioritized over Seerr events to reduce duplicate processing.

docs.title: Monitored items
docs.text:
Only items that are Monitored in Sonarr/Radarr are downloaded. This always applies, on every path (polling, Seerr, Sonarr and Radarr webhooks), and there is nothing to configure.

  • An unmonitored movie, series or episode is skipped. The queue shows the reason (Radarr movie is unmonitored / Sonarr episode is unmonitored).
  • The state is re-checked live right before each download, so un-monitoring something after it was queued is enough to cancel it.
  • Queued items that are not started yet are skipped automatically when they become unmonitored. A download already in progress is allowed to finish.
  • If Sonarr/Radarr cannot be reached for the check, the item is treated as monitored and is not blocked.

docs.title: Provider selection
docs.text:
VibraVid determines which provider to use for each item through two mechanisms — you can use one or both.

Method 1 — Per-item tag (advanced, requires tagging each title)

Add a tag directly to the movie or series in Sonarr/Radarr using the format provider-<site>. VibraVid reads the tag at download time and uses that provider regardless of the fallback list. This is useful when specific titles are only available on a particular service.

Tags are created in Sonarr/Radarr under Settings -> Tags, then assigned to individual series or movies from their edit page.

Tag Behaviour provider-animeunity Uses AnimeUnity for that title provider-<site> Uses any supported VibraVid site for that title hold / pausa Skips the item until the tag is removed skip-s1, skip-s2, ... Skips a specific season of a series

Method 2 — Global fallback list (recommended, zero per-title configuration)

Configure provider_fallback with an ordered list of providers. VibraVid tries them in sequence and stops at the first that finds a matching title. No tagging required — add as many providers as you want as safety nets.

Recommended full configuration (covers general content, anime, and niche services):

provider_fallback = [
    "streamingcommunity",
    "animeunity",
    "discoveryplus",
    "aurora",
    "mediasetinfinity",
    "raiplay",
    "animeworld",
    "crunchyroll",
    "primevideo",
    "tubitv"
]

If provider_fallback is empty or omitted, VibraVid tries streamingcommunity only and fails if the title is not found there.

Italian dub preference (download_italian_anime_default)

When true, if the selected provider returns both an original-language version and an (ITA) dubbed version of the same title, VibraVid automatically picks the Italian dub. This applies regardless of which method selected the provider.

download_italian_anime_default = true

docs.title: Path mapping — essential for split environments
docs.text:
path_mapping is one of the most important settings when Radarr/Sonarr run in Docker while VibraVid runs on the host (or vice versa). After a download completes, VibraVid must tell Radarr/Sonarr exactly where the file is so they can import it. If the two services see the same physical folder under different paths, Radarr/Sonarr will receive a path they cannot resolve and the import will fail.

Setup path_mapping needed? Both on bare metal No Both in Docker with identical volume mounts No VibraVid on host, ARR stack in Docker Yes Both in Docker with different volume mounts Yes

Example: VibraVid on the host sees /media/Media/Film. Radarr's Docker Compose mounts the same folder at a different path:

volumes:
  - /media/Media/Film:/media/Film
  - /media/Media/Anime:/media/Anime
  - /media/Media/Series:/media/Series

Without path_mapping, VibraVid reports /media/Media/Film/my-movie to Radarr. Radarr looks for that path inside its container — it does not exist there — and the import fails. With the mapping configured, VibraVid automatically translates the path before every API call:

[ARR.path_mapping]
"/media/Media/Film"   = "/media/Film"
"/media/Media/Anime"  = "/media/Anime"
"/media/Media/Series" = "/media/Series"

Each key is a prefix as seen by VibraVid; the value is the equivalent prefix inside the Radarr/Sonarr container. Entries are checked in order and the first matching prefix is replaced. Leave path_mapping as {} when both services share the same filesystem view.

docs.title: Season mapping (Sonarr → provider)
docs.text:
Sonarr and the provider sometimes number the same series differently (e.g. Sonarr S17, provider S14). VibraVid fixes this automatically, with no configuration, when a TMDB_API_KEY is set:

  • Missing TMDB id: if Sonarr has none, VibraVid finds it on TMDB by matching the season's air dates with Sonarr's.
  • Conflicting ids: if Sonarr's TMDB id and the one behind its TVDB id differ, the one that airs the same episodes on the same days is used. If neither or both do, the download is refused.
  • Season not on the provider: the TMDB episode titles are matched with the provider's seasons to find the right season and episode (Sonarr S17E02 → provider S14E02).

The file is downloaded with the provider's numbering, renamed to Sonarr's (S17E02) and imported into the right episode. If the provider has no such season and the match is not clear, the episode is skipped (season_not_available) instead of downloading a different season. Anime providers are excluded: they have one entry per season.

docs.title: Sonarr workflow
docs.text:
For series, VibraVid ARR can:

  • read missing episodes from Sonarr;
  • resolve series, season and episode metadata;
  • download the requested episode into the expected series path;
  • trigger a Sonarr rescan/import;
  • verify whether the episode was imported;
  • optionally mark the episode as unmonitored after successful import.

docs.title: Radarr workflow
docs.text:
For movies, VibraVid ARR can:

  • read missing movies from Radarr;
  • resolve title, year and TMDB metadata;
  • download the requested movie into the expected movie path;
  • trigger a Radarr rescan/import;
  • verify whether the movie was imported;
  • optionally mark the movie as unmonitored after successful import.

docs.title: Naming and folder structure — always delegated to Sonarr/Radarr
docs.text:
VibraVid never invents its own filename/folder scheme for imported media. After a download completes it calls Sonarr/Radarr's own Rescan/ManualImport/Rename commands, so the final file on disk always follows your naming configuration in Sonarr/Radarr (Settings -> Media Management), not a VibraVid-specific format.

Warning

Sonarr's "Rename Episodes" and Radarr's "Rename Movies" options (Settings -> Media Management) are disabled by default on a clean Sonarr/Radarr install. If left disabled, imported files still land correctly in your library, but keep VibraVid's raw scraped filename instead of your configured naming format (no S01E01, no year, etc). Enable "Rename Episodes" / "Rename Movies" in Sonarr/Radarr if you want clean, consistent filenames. VibraVid logs a one-time warning per ARR sync when it detects this setting is off.

To enable it, open Sonarr/Radarr -> Settings -> Media Management, turn on Rename Episodes (Sonarr) or Rename Movies (Radarr) in the naming section, then Save. Renaming only works if Sonarr/Radarr can write to the media folder: run VibraVid with the same PUID/PGID as Sonarr/Radarr, otherwise the rename fails with Permission denied and the raw filename stays.

docs.title: Recommended setup
docs.text:
Use shared volumes so VibraVid and Sonarr/Radarr see the same filesystem paths. If containers use different internal paths for the same media folder, imports may fail because Sonarr/Radarr will not find the downloaded files.

Example Docker path layout:

/media
├── movies
├── series
└── downloads

Mount the same media root into VibraVid, Sonarr and Radarr whenever possible.

docs.title: Basics
docs.text:
python manual.py -h                                                       # help + available sites
python manual.py -i streamingcommunity --search "interstellar"            # search and download
python manual.py -i streamingcommunity --search "interstellar" --item 0   # pick a result (0-based) without prompting
python manual.py -i 0 --search "interstellar"                             # site by index number
python manual.py -i streamingcommunity --search "interstellar" --skip-ts  # skip TS/CAM (StreamingCommunity only)
python manual.py -i streamingcommunity --search "interstellar" --no-log   # no log file for this run
python manual.py --dep                                                    # show dependency paths

Site index numbers follow the services that are switched on: services listed in hidden_services are not loaded and the others are renumbered without gaps, so check -h for the current numbers (names never change).

docs.title: Series and year
docs.text:
--season / --episode skip the prompts. Values: a number, a range "1-5", or "*" for all.

python manual.py -i streamingcommunity --search "breaking bad" --item 0 --season 1 --episode 3
python manual.py -i streamingcommunity --search "breaking bad" --item 0 --season 1 --episode "1-5"
python manual.py -i streamingcommunity --search "breaking bad" --item 0 --season 1 --episode "*"   # whole season
python manual.py -i streamingcommunity --search "breaking bad" --item 0 --season "*"               # all seasons
python manual.py -i streamingcommunity --search "breaking bad" --item 0 --season "1-3"

python manual.py -i streamingcommunity --search "dune" --year 2021          # exact year
python manual.py -i streamingcommunity --search "batman" --year "1990-2015" # range

docs.title: Track selection and output
docs.text:
python manual.py ... -sv 1080                  # video
python manual.py ... -sa "eng"                 # audio language (long form: --audio-langs)
python manual.py ... -ss "eng"                 # subtitles (long form: --sub-langs)
python manual.py ... -ss "ita_forced"          # only the forced subtitle track
python manual.py ... -sa "deu" --skip-no-match # skip the whole download if the filter matches no track
python manual.py ... --extension mp4           # container (overrides PROCESS.extension for this run)

Full filter syntax: Stream selection filters.

docs.title: Console, proxy, progress
docs.text:
python manual.py --close-console false                                # keep the console open (loop mode)
python manual.py -i ... --close-console true                          # close it after the download

python manual.py -i ... --use_proxy                                   # configured proxy, default scope
python manual.py -i ... --use_proxy --proxy-scope down                # only downloads (Velora)
python manual.py -i ... --use_proxy --proxy-scope scrap               # only scraping

python manual.py -i ... --plain-progress                              # one line per track every 5s, e.g.
#   Vid [H.264] 720p 2.4 Mbps  28%  290.2M / 1012.7M  65.27M/s  ETA 00:11
python manual.py -i ... --plain-progress --progress-interval 2        # every 2s
python manual.py -i ... --no-progress                                 # no progress output

docs.title: Metadata sidecars
docs.text:
.nfo + artwork for Jellyfin/Emby/Kodi, only for a reliable match; off by default (DOWNLOAD.write_sidecars). See Metadata providers.

python manual.py -i ... --sidecars                                    # TMDB, then IMDb
python manual.py -i ... --sidecars --metadata-provider imdb           # IMDb only, no key
python manual.py -i ... --sidecars --metadata-provider tvdb,tmdb      # needs TVDB_API_KEY or Provider.tvdb
python manual.py -i ... --no-sidecars                                 # off for this run

docs.title: Direct download (--down)
docs.text:
Download from a URL, skipping site search. Type is auto-detected (MP4 / HLS / DASH / ISM) or forced with --type.

# MP4 / auto-detected
python manual.py --down "https://example.com/video.mp4" -o "./Video/clip.mp4"

# HLS with a known key
python manual.py --down "https://example.com/master.m3u8" --type hls --key "<KID>:<KEY>" -o "./Video/movie.mkv"

# DASH + Widevine license server (--license-headers adds headers for the license request; repeatable like --headers)
python manual.py --down "https://example.com/manifest.mpd" --type dash \
  --license-url "https://example.com/wv/license" --drm widevine \
  --headers "Authorization: Bearer <token>" --license-headers "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -o "./Video/movie.mkv"

# Only a clip: segments 10-50, or a time range
python manual.py --down "https://example.com/master.m3u8" --type hls --max-segments "10-50" -o "./Video/clip.mkv"
python manual.py --down "https://example.com/master.m3u8" --type hls --max-time "00:01:00-00:05:00" -o "./Video/clip.mkv"

docs.title: Custom JSON manifest
docs.text:
--down also takes a .json file/URL containing "vibravid_manifest" (auto-detected, no --type) for sources without a real manifest:

{
  "vibravid_manifest": true,
  "base_url": "https://cdn.example.com/movie/",
  "duration": 5410.0,
  "tracks": [
    {
      "type": "video", "id": "v1", "codecs": "avc1.640028",
      "width": 1920, "height": 1080, "bitrate": 4500000,
      "init": "init_video.mp4",
      "segments": {"template": "chunk_video_$Number$.m4s", "start": 1, "end": 1352, "duration": 4.0}
    },
    {
      "type": "audio", "id": "a1", "language": "eng", "codecs": "mp4a.40.2",
      "init": "init_audio.mp4",
      "segments": {"list": ["seg0.m4s", "seg1.m4s", "seg2.m4s"]}
    }
  ]
}

python manual.py --down "https://example.com/manifest.json" -o "./Video/movie.mkv"
segments mode Fields Behaviour list URLs, or objects with url/size/duration/range explicit list template template, start, step (or duration), end (or count) DASH-style $Number$ / $Time$ / $RepresentationID$ expansion ranges / chunk url + ranges array, or chunk + size to auto-split byte ranges of a single file

init is a URL string, an object (url, range) or inline base64 (data). Placeholders support zero-padding ($Number%05d$); $$ is a literal $.

docs.title: Export and import (--export, --import)
docs.text:
--export [FILE] resolves the tracks and keys like a normal run but does not download: it writes the result to a JSON file (default .cache/export/<site>_<type>_<title>.json). --import FILE downloads every entry of such a file, in sequence, with no search and (when the keys were exported) no CDM. Both work for MP4, HLS, DASH and ISM, from --down or from a service search (-i SITE -s QUERY --export).

python manual.py --down "https://example.com/master.m3u8" --key "<KID>:<KEY>" --export ./movie.json
python manual.py --import ./movie.json              # add -o to pick the output name (single entry)

docs.title: Metadata for a direct download (--meta-*)
docs.text:
A plain --down has no title context, so title-dependent hooks and Vault upload/lookup are skipped. --meta-* attaches it (--resolve-only sets these automatically):

python manual.py --down "https://example.com/master.m3u8" --type hls --key "<KID>:<KEY>" \
  -o "./Video/Movie (2024)/movie.mkv" --meta-title "Movie Name" --meta-type Film --meta-site streamingcommunity

python manual.py --down "..." --type hls --key "<KID>:<KEY>" -o "./Video/Show/Season 01/episode.mkv" \
  --meta-title "Show Name" --meta-type TV --meta-season 1 --meta-episode 3

docs.title: yt-dlp (--yt-dlp)
docs.text:
Any site yt-dlp supports (separate from --down, which is for HLS/DASH/ISM/MP4 URLs).

python manual.py --yt-dlp "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=..." -o "./Video/clip.mp4"
python manual.py --yt-dlp "<URL>" --extract-audio --audio-format mp3 --audio-quality 0
Flag Effect --yt-dlp <URL> Download with yt-dlp instead of the site-search/--down flow --format <SPEC> Format selector (default bestvideo+bestaudio/best) --list-formats List formats and exit --interactive-format Show formats and prompt for the format ID --extract-audio Audio only --audio-format <FORMAT> mp3, m4a, wav, opus, ... --audio-quality <QUALITY> 0, 5, 8k, ... --playlist-end <N> Only the first N playlist entries --sub-langs <LANGS> Subtitle languages (it,en); same flag as -ss --write-subs / --write-auto-subs Write subtitles / auto-generated subtitles

docs.title: Advanced options
docs.text:
Flag Effect --use-curl-cffi Download segments via curl_cffi (browser TLS impersonation) instead of Velora, for Cloudflare-protected segments --http-version {1.1,2,3} Force the HTTP version -o, --output <PATH> Output path for --down / --yt-dlp --clear Delete the cached login/session tokens of the service given with -i (requires -i; never touches other services or login.toml) --key <KID:KEY> Hex decryption key, repeatable. With --down or a service run (-i 0 --key <KID>:<KEY>): used instead of the vault/CDM for the KIDs it covers, other KIDs resolve normally --no-vault-cache Bypass the vault cache; fresh CDM license request every run --cdm <CDM> CDM for this run, above login.toml and config.toml: a .wvd/.prd name, search, or a remote CDM id. Repeatable, one per DRM system (--cdm mine.wvd --cdm my_playready). A JSON list/table is accepted for quality rules. Unknown file/id stops the run before downloading --no-decrypt Debug: no decryption at all (in-flight or post-download) --no-livemux / --livemux Disable / force the streaming-mux fast path (off by default: turn it on with process in login.toml or PROCESS.use_live_mux) --no-live-decrypt Disable in-flight (per-segment) decryption for this run: segments are decrypted after the download. It is on only with process.live_decrypt / DOWNLOAD.use_live_decrypt (process in login.toml, DOWNLOAD.use_live_decrypt) --no-concurrent Download video, audio and subtitles sequentially (concurrent by default) --skip-no-match Skip the download if -sv/-sa/-ss match no track, instead of falling back to the best --log-decryptor-output Write flux's stdout/stderr to the log, tagged with the engine name (e.g. [FLUX]) --abc Anonymize printed KID:KEY pairs (alternating characters masked with ?) --hls-method AES_128\|NONE Override the HLS encryption method, ignoring #EXT-X-KEY (or supplying it). NONE = clear segments; AES_128 = AES-128-CBC (pair with --hls-key/--hls-iv) --hls-key <HEX\|BASE64\|FILE> Raw AES-128 key instead of fetching the manifest's URI= --hls-iv <HEX> IV instead of the manifest's IV=0x... (or the implicit per-segment IV) --skip-content-check Skip the HEAD content-type check for MP4 downloads (--type mp4), for single-use URLs --skip-sanitize Use -o verbatim (no transliteration of non-ASCII characters) --no-manifest-info Don't print the manifest/streams table --binary-update Check FFmpeg/Flux/Packager/dovi_tool/MKVToolNix/Velora against AstraeLabs/Binary and re-download outdated ones (the CLI also does it every 2 days: auto_update_binaries) --resolve-only Resolve and cache manifest/keys/license/playlist without downloading (pairs with the queue) --export [FILE] Resolve tracks and keys, write them to a JSON file instead of downloading (see Export and import) --import <FILE> Download every entry of a file written by --export, no search and no CDM when the keys were exported --tui Launch the Textual terminal UI -UP, --update Auto-update to the latest release (binary builds only) --check-update Print how to update for your installation (binary, source, Docker) and exit --skip-update-check Skip the background startup check (cached 24h; failures retried after 30 min); auto_check_update = false in config.toml turns it off for good --version Print the version and exit 
# Manual AES-128 override (manifest without its own #EXT-X-KEY)
python manual.py --down "https://example.com/master.m3u8" --type hls --hls-method AES_128 \
  --hls-key "0011223344556677889900112233445566" --hls-iv "00000000000000000000000000000001" -o "./Video/clip.mkv"

docs.title: Default options for a service
docs.text: python manual.py -i <service> --help lists a service's options; args in login.toml sets permanent defaults for them (details).

docs.title: Download queue (--queue-*)
docs.text:
python manual.py -i streamingcommunity --search "interstellar" --item 0 --queue-add   # queue instead of downloading
python manual.py --down "https://example.com/movie.mkv" -o "./Video/movie.mkv" --queue-add
python manual.py --queue-list
python manual.py --queue-remove <ID>
python manual.py --queue-clear
python manual.py --queue-run                       # process every pending/interrupted item in order

Note

Only invocations that complete without any prompt can be queued; ambiguous ones (--global, a site search without --item) are rejected when enqueued.

Items enqueued together share an auto-generated queue name (e.g. 20260723-152525, shown by --queue-list). Pass it to target one batch:

python manual.py --queue-run 20260723-152525       # also --queue-list / --queue-clear <name>
python manual.py --queue-run --queue-ids abc12345,def67890   # only these item ids (see --queue-list)
python manual.py --queue-select                    # pick the queue from a numbered list

docs.title: Global search
docs.text:
python manual.py --global -s "cars"
python manual.py --category 1    # Anime   (2: Movies & Series, 3: Series only, 4: Movies only)

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Settings live in Conf/config.toml (one section per block below). ARR settings: ARR Integration.

docs.title: TMDB API Key
docs.text:
Optional. A free TMDB key unlocks the %(tmdb_*), %(original_title), %(original_language) and %(imdb_id) filename tokens, poster/backdrop artwork (embed_poster) and strict TMDB/TVDB matching in ARR. Without it the tokens are dropped from filenames and artwork/matching falls back to the site's own data. One key serves CLI, TUI, GUI and ARR.

Set the TMDB_API_KEY environment variable before running:

export TMDB_API_KEY=your_key_here        # PowerShell: $env:TMDB_API_KEY = "your_key_here"
python manual.py                         # CLI (python tui.py / python GUI/manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8000)
  • Docker / NAS: set it in .env (see .env.example).
  • GUI: no in-app field; the key is read at process start, so restart the server/container after changing it. Without it, search shows a "TMDB covers aren't active" hint.
  • Deprecated: [Provider] tmdb = "..." in Conf/login.toml still works as a fallback (logs a warning) but will be removed.
  • login.toml can hold secrets: don't commit your copy.

docs.title: Metadata providers
docs.text:
With write_sidecars (DOWNLOAD) VibraVid writes the files Jellyfin, Emby and Kodi read (Plex ignores them) next to each download. Fields a provider lacks are left out.

Media Files Film <name>.nfo, <name>-poster.jpg, <name>-fanart.jpg Episode <name>.nfo, <name>-thumb.jpg (episode still) Series tvshow.nfo, poster.jpg, fanart.jpg, season01-poster.jpg in the show folder (parent of the season folder); written once, only missing parts are added later Provider Film Episode Series TMDB title, original title, year, premiere date, rating + votes, tagline, plot, runtime, age rating (IT, else US), genres, keywords, countries, studios, collection, directors, writers, 15 actors (role, photo), YouTube trailer, poster, fanart title, air date, plot, runtime, rating + votes, directors, writers, guest stars, still title, original title, year, status, rating + votes, plot, age rating, runtime, genres, networks, 15 actors, poster, fanart, season posters IMDb same, no fanart (trailer is an IMDb page) same, from the episode's own record same, no fanart or season posters TVDB same, no rating/votes title, air date, plot, runtime, still no rating; poster, fanart, cast, networks, age rating, status

metadata_provider (DEFAULT) is one name or an ordered list; the first provider with a reliable match wins, unavailable ones (no key) are skipped.

Provider Key Language Notes tmdb TMDB_API_KEY (above) Italian Best matching; only one that remaps anime absolute numbering imdb none English Italian titles are found only if the site supplies a TMDB id and a TMDB key is set tvdb TVDB_API_KEY Italian when translated Needs a TheTVDB key 
python manual.py ... --metadata-provider tmdb,imdb   # default
python manual.py ... --metadata-provider imdb        # no key needed

TVDB key: the TVDB_API_KEY environment variable (wins; Docker/NAS: .env), or in Conf/login.toml (a supported location, unlike TMDB's):

[Provider]
tvdb = "your_key_here"

docs.title: Default options for a service (args)
docs.text:
Every service section in Conf/login.toml has an args key (empty by default), added to every download of that service and written like on the command line:

[nowtvit]
args = "--quality 1080 --range HDR10"

[chili]
args = "--country es"

docs.title: Pipeline switches for a service (process)
docs.text:
A service section of Conf/login.toml switches two parts of the download pipeline on or off for that service only, without touching the service itself. Without a process line both are off (the old _live_mux flag of the services is no longer read):

[disney]
process = { live_mux = true, live_decrypt = true }
Switch true false or unset live_mux Streaming-mux fast path: the final .mkv is written while downloading Tracks are muxed after the download live_decrypt In-flight (per-segment) decryption Segments are decrypted after the download (slower). The streaming mux then only runs when no selected track is encrypted

A switch missing from process falls back to the global one in config.toml (PROCESS.use_live_mux, DOWNLOAD.use_live_decrypt, both false by default), so services without a login.toml section (e.g. raiplay) follow config.toml. For a single run: --livemux forces the streaming mux, --no-livemux and --no-live-decrypt switch it off. Order: command line, then process in login.toml, then config.toml. A JSON string (process = '{"live_mux": false}') or a [disney.process] table work too.

auto_check_update = true

docs.title: Format tokens
docs.text:
Defaults: movie_format = "%(title_name) (%(title_year))/%(title_name) (%(title_year))", episode_format = "%(series_name)/S%(season:02d)/%(episode_name) S%(season:02d)E%(episode:02d)" (e.g. Breaking Bad/S01/Pilot S01E05.mkv). / separates folders from the filename.

Token Movie Episode Description %(title_name), %(title_name_slug) x Movie title (slug) %(title_year) x Release year (omitted if unavailable) %(series_name), %(series_name_slug) x Series name (slug) %(series_year) x Series release year %(season:FORMAT), %(episode:FORMAT) x Season / episode number with padding %(episode_name), %(episode_name_slug) x Episode title (sanitized / slug) %(absolute:FORMAT) x Absolute episode number, anime only (AnimeUnity/AnimeWorld) %(quality), %(language) x x Video resolution, audio languages %(video_codec), %(audio_codec) x x Codecs %(audio_flags), %(sub_flags) x x Track flags, e.g. DEFAULT, CC-SDH-FORCED %(fps), %(video_bitrate) x x Frame rate and average video bit rate of the muxed file, e.g. 23.976fps, 1212kbps %(hdr), %(bit_depth) x x HDR10, HDR10+, HLG or DV (empty for SDR); video bit depth, e.g. 10bit %(audio_channels) x x Channels of the first audio track, e.g. 2.0, 5.1 %(original_title), %(original_language) x x Original title / language code (e.g. ja) (TMDB key) %(tmdb_id), %(tmdb_title), %(imdb_id) x x TMDB id, TMDB title in the lookup language, IMDb id e.g. tt0409591 (TMDB key) %(tmdb_episode_title) x TMDB episode title, from tmdb_id + season/episode (TMDB key) %(tmdb_season_number:FORMAT) x Real TMDB season number, mapped from absolute/flat numbers when needed (anime) (TMDB key) %(tmdb_season_name) x TMDB season name, e.g. Season 2, mapped the same way (TMDB key)

Padding (season, episode, absolute, tmdb_season_number, track_number): %(season:02d) -> 01, %(season:03d) -> 001, %(season:d) -> 1.

Tokens that can't be resolved (no TMDB key, absolute on non-anime) are removed together with any surrounding []/().

song_format (default "%(album)/%(track_number:02d). %(title)" -> Discovery/01. One More Time.mp3): %(artist), %(artist_slug), %(album), %(album_slug), %(title), %(title_slug), %(year) (omitted if unavailable), %(track_number:FORMAT).

tag_format (default "[VibraVid]"): prefix written in the title and comment tags ([VibraVid] Inception), both by the final retag and the merge -metadata flags. "" disables tagging; any other text replaces the prefix.

Recommended with a TMDB key:

movie_format = "%(title_name) (%(title_year)) [%(tmdb_id)]/%(title_name) (%(title_year)) [%(tmdb_title)] [%(quality)]"
episode_format = "%(series_name) [%(tmdb_id)]/S%(tmdb_season_number:02d) - %(tmdb_season_name)/%(episode_name) - %(tmdb_episode_title) S%(season:02d)E%(episode:02d) [%(tmdb_title)] [%(quality)]"

CLI: --max-speed subtitle_resolve_workers 4 HLS subtitle renditions resolved concurrently; 1 = sequential extract_embedded_cc false HLS only: extract embedded CEA-608/708 captions (EXT-X-MEDIA:TYPE=CLOSED-CAPTIONS) into a subtitle track. Opt-in: needs decoding the whole video (extra time/CPU) cleanup_tmp_folder true Remove temporary files afterwards temp_root "" Folder for the temporary files (segments, merge and decrypt leftovers). Empty = next to the output file. With the output on a NAS share, point it to a fast local disk: every step otherwise reads and writes the whole title over the network (about 8x the file size). Needs about 2x the size of one title. The VIBRAVID_TEMP_DIR environment variable overrides it (the Docker image sets it to /app/tmp) embed_poster false Embed a poster/still: matching TMDB artwork, else the site's own write_sidecars false Write .nfo + poster/thumb next to each download when the match is reliable (see Metadata providers). CLI: --sidecars / --no-sidecars use_live_decrypt false In-flight (per-segment) decryption while downloading, for every service without its own process line in login.toml. false = decrypt after the download (per run: --no-live-decrypt) use_curl_cffi_segments false Download segments via curl_cffi (TLS/JA3 impersonation) instead of Velora segment_delay_seconds 0 Fixed delay before each segment request (CDN rate limits) segment_delay_jitter_seconds 0 Random 0..N seconds added on top of the delay live_max_empty_polls 8 Live HLS/DASH: consecutive polls without new segments (or failures) before the stream is considered ended max_token_refresh_rounds 10 Retry rounds when segments fail mid-download (expired token -> 403, transient 503): fresh manifest/token, retry only failed segments token_refresh_backoff_seconds 4.0 Wait = backoff x round, capped at 20s token_refresh_stall_rounds 3 Give up after this many consecutive rounds without progress

docs.title: Stream selection filters
docs.text:
select_video, select_audio and select_subtitle choose which tracks are downloaded.

Video

Value Description "best" / "worst" Best / worst resolution "hybrid" Best HDR (non-DV) base + worst Dolby Vision companion "1080" Exact height (falls back to worst) "1080,H265" Height + codec "1080\|best", "1080\|best,H265" Same, falling back to best "b=8000:f=best" Bitrate cap (kbps); useful when the top rendition isn't decryptable with your CDM level "b=1000-8000:f=best", "b=1000-:f=best" Bitrate range / floor only "false" Skip video

Native key=value filters combine constraints with :: r= resolution, c= codec, b= bitrate, i= manifest id (regex), f= fallback (best/worst/all), e.g. "r=1080:c=hvc1:f=best".

Audio

Value Description If not found "best" / "worst" Best / worst bitrate per language Best / worst across all "all" All tracks Downloads all "default" / "non-default" Streams marked / not marked default DROP "ita" Italian DROP "ita\|it" Pipe-separated languages DROP if none "ita,MP4A" Language + codec DROP "ita\|best", "ita\|best,AAC" Language (+ codec) with fallback Falls back to best "b=64-192:f=best" Bitrate range (kbps) Ignores range "1ita\|2eng" Numbered slots, exclusive priority Skips the whole download "false" Skip audio n/a

Same native keys as video plus l= language, e.g. "l=ita:c=aac:f=best".

Subtitle: "all", "default", "non-default", "ita|eng" (languages), "ita_forced" (flags forced, cc, sdh), "ita_forced|eng_cc", "false".

CLI: --log-decryptor-output vault - External key store(s), queried before CDM extraction

docs.title: Multiple / self-hosted DRM vaults
docs.text:
One [DRM.vault.<name>] table per vault, queried in declaration order until every KID is resolved.

[DRM.vault.myvault]
url = "https://drm.example.com"
token = "..."
protocol = "custom"

[DRM.vault.query_vault]
url = "https://keys.example.net/"
username = "user"
password = "..."
protocol = "query"
protocol Request Writes custom POST {url}/get-keys / POST {url}/save-keys (the default vault's contract) yes api GET {url}/{service}/{kid}, Bearer token only with save_keys json POST {url} {"method", "params", "token"} (JSON-RPC) only with save_keys query GET {url}?service=&kid=&username=&password= no
  • protocol is optional: auto-detected once and cached in .cache/services/vault/universal_<name>.json (delete to re-detect).
  • default (old name vault_1) is the built-in vault, logged as claudio. Resolved keys show kid:key | *claudio [1] (vault name + position).
  • New keys are written back to custom vaults, and to api/json ones only with save_keys = true (default false).
  • When flux proves a stored key wrong, the vault that returned it gets the corrected key (one key per KID, warning counter reset). The default vault keeps the old one in drm_keys_replaced.
  • Vaults that publish a service list are queried under the matching service, then generic; others under generic.
  • A vault answering 429 is skipped for the requested retry_after.
  • Optional fields: service (force a namespace), timeout (seconds, default 10).

Conf/config.toml is tracked by git: don't commit third-party vault tokens.

docs.title: Remote CDMs
docs.text:
Declare once under [DRM.remote_cdm.<id>]; the id is free text (not search/default) and is what you put in cdm.

[DRM.remote_cdm.my_widevine]
device_type = "ANDROID"
system_id = 22590
security_level = 3
host = "https://cdrm-project.com/remotecdm/widevine"
secret = "CDRM"
device_name = "public"

[DRM.remote_cdm.my_playready]
device_name = "public"
security_level = 3000
host = "https://cdrm-project.com/remotecdm/playready"
secret = "CDRM"
Key Widevine PlayReady Description device_type x "ANDROID" or "CHROME" system_id x Widevine system ID (default 22590 for Android) security_level x x Widevine 1-3; PlayReady e.g. 3000 for SL3000 host x x Remote CDM server URL secret x x Authentication secret device_name x x Device registered on the remote service

The system (Widevine/PlayReady) is inferred: device_type or type = "custom_api_1" = Widevine, a device_name starting with SL = PlayReady, no device_type = PlayReady. Set system = "widevine" / "playready" to force it.

docs.title: Hosted remote CDM API
docs.text:
A third-party hosted CDM (Widevine and PlayReady) over HTTP: same [DRM.remote_cdm.<id>] table with type = "custom_api_1", plus host and secret from your provider.

[DRM.remote_cdm.hosted_widevine]
type = "custom_api_1"
host = "YOUR_PROVIDER_API_URL"
secret = "YOUR_PROVIDER_API_KEY"
device_name = "L3"
Key Default Description type - Must be "custom_api_1" (otherwise a standard pywidevine/pyplayready remote CDM) host, secret required Provider API URL and key device_name ChromeCDM Widevine: ChromeCDM, L1, L2, L3. PlayReady: SL2, SL3 auth_header x-api-key Header the provider expects the key in service_name - Optional service tag

docs.title: Choosing the CDM (cdm)
docs.text:
cdm picks the CDM that extracts keys. Set it in [DRM] of config.toml (default for all services) and/or in a service section of login.toml (that service only). Each system (Widevine, PlayReady) uses exactly one CDM at a time: a local device file or a remote CDM.

cdm entry Meaning "search" First .wvd (Widevine) and .prd (PlayReady) in the binary folder (Local CDM devices) ends with .wvd / .prd That file, looked up in wvd/ or prd/ "default" login.toml only: use [DRM]'s cdm (cdm = "" means the same) anything else Id of a remote CDM from DRM.remote_cdm

The value is one entry or a list with one entry per system. Per system the order is: service cdm in login.toml, then [DRM], then "search" (a service naming only a .wvd keeps the [DRM] choice for PlayReady). A missing file or unknown id stops the download with an error listing the known ids. The CLI --cdm (cli) wins over both for one run.

# config.toml: default for everyone
[DRM]
cdm = ["my_widevine", "my_playready.prd"]

# login.toml: this service uses a local Widevine file, PlayReady stays as in [DRM]
[mysite]
cdm = "mine.wvd"

CDM by video quality: a list entry can be a table limited to a height range, with min_height / max_height (inclusive, both optional) and a cdm (any entry above, or a list). Per system the first matching entry wins; an entry without limits always matches, so put it last. The height compared is the tallest selected video (0 for audio only), since one manifest uses one license session. No match falls through to the next level ([DRM], then "search").

[mysite]
cdm = [
  { min_height = 1080, cdm = "my_l1_remote" },
  { cdm = "device_l3.wvd" },
]

Which CDM was used: each key request prints one line: device file name (no path) with SysID (.wvd) or Model (.prd), or remote + device name, and why it was picked. The security level and full path go to the log file.

[+] device_l3.wvd | SysID: 22594 | why: search
[+] tv_sl3000.prd | Model: TPV AOC 50U6185 | why: config.toml [DRM]
[+] remote L1 | why: login.toml 'mysite', min_height 1080
After why: Meaning --cdm Command line login.toml '<service>' (+ , min_height 1080 for quality rules) The service's own cdm config.toml [DRM] [DRM]'s default cdm search First device file in the binary folder

Startup check: every cdm (--cdm, each service in login.toml, [DRM]) is validated at startup regardless of height. A missing file, unknown remote id, reserved id (search, default) or malformed quality rule is warned right away. A wrong --cdm stops the run; mistakes in the files only warn (non-DRM downloads need no CDM).

Note

prefer_remote_cdm and the inline [DRM.widevine] / [DRM.playready] blocks no longer exist: declare the remote CDM under [DRM.remote_cdm.<id>] and select it with cdm.

docs.title: Local CDM devices
docs.text:
Put device files in the binary directory (override with VIBRAVID_BINARY_DIR, e.g. /home/user_name/.local/bin/binary):

Platform Binary directory Windows C:\binary\VibraVid Linux ~/.local/bin/binary/VibraVid macOS ~/Applications/binary/VibraVid
  • tools/: executables (ffmpeg, yt-dlp, velora, flux, ...) and .versions.json
  • wvd/: Widevine .wvd files (pywidevine)
  • prd/: PlayReady .prd files (pyplayready)

Downloaded binaries are only used from tools/; .wvd/.prd files left in the old flat location (C:\binary, ~/.local/bin/binary, ~/Applications/binary) are still found. With cdm = "search" the first .wvd/.prd is used; to keep several, name one, e.g. cdm = "mine.wvd".

docs.title: Recommended: Docker Compose
docs.text:
docker-compose up -d        # Start
docker-compose logs -f      # View logs
docker-compose down         # Stop (data persists)

For NAS users (Synology, TrueNAS, Unraid, etc.), see the NAS deployment guide for a step-by-step setup guide including bind mounts and permission configuration.

docs.title: Custom paths and ports
docs.text:
Copy the provided template and edit the values you need:

cp .env.example .env

Key variables (full list in .env.example):

Variable Default Description VIBRAVID_PORT 8000 Host port exposed by the container VIBRAVID_VIDEO_DIR named volume Where downloads land on the host (e.g. /volume2/Movies) VIBRAVID_DB_DIR named volume Host path for the SQLite database VIBRAVID_CONFIG_DIR named volume Host path for config.toml / login.toml VIBRAVID_LOGS_DIR named volume Host path for application logs ALLOWED_HOSTS localhost,127.0.0.1 Comma-separated hostnames Django accepts CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS http://localhost:8000,... Origins for CSRF validation PUID / PGID unset User/group ID the container process runs as — set these to your host user's id -u/id -g so downloaded files aren't owned by root (see the NAS guide for the full walkthrough) VIBRAVID_HIDDEN_SITES unset Comma-separated service folder names to switch off (CLI, TUI and GUI), added to hidden_services in config.toml (see Configuration). Uncomment it in docker-compose.yml WATCHLIST_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECONDS 14400 (4h) Initial interval (min 900) of the watchlist auto-download loop. An interval saved from the GUI's Watchlist page takes precedence after that

docs.title: Optional sidecar (Telegram bot)
docs.text:
The Telegram bot is an opt-in Compose service behind the telegram profile (docker-compose --profile telegram up -d) — see that guide for its own environment variables.

NAS example — store downloads on a NAS share, expose on port 9000:

VIBRAVID_PORT=9000
VIBRAVID_VIDEO_DIR=/volume2/Movies
VIBRAVID_DB_DIR=/volume1/docker/vibravid/db
VIBRAVID_CONFIG_DIR=/volume1/docker/vibravid/conf
VIBRAVID_LOGS_DIR=/volume1/docker/vibravid/logs
ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost,127.0.0.1,192.168.1.100
CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=http://192.168.1.100:9000

Then start normally: 

docker-compose up -d

docs.text:
Uncomment and edit the environment section in docker-compose.yml:

environment:

  ALLOWED_HOSTS: "streaming.example.local,localhost,127.0.0.1,192.168.1.50"
  CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS: "https://streaming.example.local"
  USE_X_FORWARDED_HOST: "true"
  SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER_ENABLED: "true"
  CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE: "true"
  SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE: "true"
  DJANGO_SECRET_KEY: "your-secure-secret-key-here"
