docs.title: Updating (Docker)
docs.text:
When a new version is released, VibraVid shows an update banner in the web UI. Click Update now to update in place.

One-click update requires the Docker socket to be mounted (it is in the default docker-compose.yml):

volumes:
  - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock

With the socket mounted, Update now drives the host Docker daemon directly: it launches a short-lived helper container that runs docker compose pull && docker compose up -d, pulling the published image (ghcr.io/astraelabs/vibravid:latest) and recreating the container. No host-side script is required.

Security note

Mounting the Docker socket grants the container control of the host Docker daemon. If you'd rather not, comment out the socket volume — the button will then tell you to update manually.

Manual update (always works, socket or not):

docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

docs.title: Web GUI
docs.text: Django web interface to search and download from the browser.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
pip install -r GUI/requirements.txt
python GUI/manage.py migrate
python GUI/manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8000

Open http://<host>:8000. For Docker/NAS use the Docker and NAS guides instead of the dev server.

docs.title: Search & download
docs.text:
• Home (/): pick a site and search.
  • Results (/search/): download, add to the watchlist, or open the series-detail view (seasons/episodes).
  • Start download (/download/): queues the movie or episodes. Track selection follows the config.toml filters, like the CLI. Tick Choose tracks manually (overrides the Quality picker) to pause the download and pick tracks in the Choose tracks panel on the Downloads page: select tracks (at least one), press Download selected tracks, or Stop to cancel. A download waiting for your choice doesn't use a concurrent-download slot. GUI only: not available for watchlist auto-downloads.
  • hidden_services in config.toml (or VIBRAVID_HIDDEN_SITES, comma-separated, for Docker) switches services off in the CLI, TUI and GUI alike (details). VIBRAVID_DISABLED_SITES is still read as an alias.

docs.title: Downloads dashboard
docs.text:
/downloads/: live queue and history (polled from api/get-downloads/). Some providers may show 0% progress while downloading.

Action Endpoint Stop a running download api/kill-download/ Remove one queued download api/remove-queued-download/ Clear all queued (active keep running) api/clear-queued-downloads/ Stop and clear the queue api/kill-and-clear-queue/ Clear history (completed/failed) api/clear-history/

docs.title: Watchlist & auto-download
docs.text:
/watchlist/ tracks series and movies and downloads new content automatically.

  • Add from search results; remove items or clear the list. Metadata (seasons, poster, TMDB id) loads in the background.
  • Update all: re-check everything now.
  • Auto-download per item (watchlist/auto/<id>): for a series, enable it on a season to download newly published episodes.
  • Run now (watchlist/auto-run/): check immediately.
  • Polling interval (watchlist/auto-interval/): 15 min, 30 min, 1 h, 2 h, 4 h (default, 14400 s), 6 h, 12 h or 24 h. Saved as DEFAULT.watchlist_interval_seconds in Conf/config.toml; it overrides the WATCHLIST_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECONDS environment variable, which only sets the initial default.
  • Preferred quality (up to 1080p) per item: an episode counts as done only when a local file of that quality exists, and the watchlist waits until the provider confirms it. Quality discovery works for StreamingCommunity only; other providers use the configured quality.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
/settings/ edits Conf/config.toml and Conf/login.toml in tabs, validates before saving and writes a .backup next to the original.

  • ARR.max_concurrent_downloads applies live; most other settings need a reload (api/reload-config/) or a restart.
  • Custom CLI options sets a service's args (details); removing them leaves args = "" in login.toml.

docs.title: Bot / remote-control API
docs.text:
api/bot/* is a JSON API for bots and scripts (used by the Telegram bot):

Endpoint Purpose POST api/bot/search/ {"query": "...", "site": "__all__" \| "__cat__:<cat>" \| "<site>"} -> results POST api/bot/seasons/ Seasons/episodes of a result POST api/bot/download/ Start a download POST api/bot/sites/ Available sites/categories POST api/bot/status/ Progress of a download POST api/bot/cancel/ Stop a download POST api/bot/logs/ Recent log lines

Set VIBRAVID_BOT_SECRET to require a matching X-VibraVid-Token header. Without it these endpoints are unauthenticated: set it before exposing the GUI beyond your LAN.

docs.title: Custom service upload
docs.text: Settings -> Providers -> Add a provider installs a site module ZIP (api/upload-service/) into VibraVid/services/<name> and reloads the registry (api/registry-status/). It only appears in the GUI dropdown if it ships GUI/searchapp/api/<service_name>.py. Uploaded providers lists your uploads, each with a Remove button (click twice to confirm); built-in services and imp_service sources can't be removed. With Docker, uploads live in the container's writable layer and are lost when it is recreated: re-upload or use an imp_service source.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text: A banner appears when a newer release exists (api/version/check/, cached 1 h); api/version/update/ applies it (Docker one-click). api/binaries/update/ is the GUI counterpart of --binary-update. api/imp-service/refresh/ (the Refresh external import button) pulls the newest commit of the imp_service repositories and reloads the services. auto_check_update = false hides the banner.

docs.title: ARR stack page
docs.text: /arr-stack/: the ARR processing queue (filter by status/source/sync) and sync trigger (api/arr/trigger-sync/). Setup: ARR Integration.

docs.title: CSRF & reverse proxy
docs.text:
Behind a reverse proxy or outside the LAN, Django may reject requests on CSRF checks. Set as needed:

Variable Use CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS="http://127.0.0.1:8000 https://yourdomain.com" Domains/ports that differ from Django's expected origin SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER_ENABLED=true Proxy terminates TLS: trust the forwarded scheme

Apache must also send RequestHeader set X-Forwarded-Proto "https".

Recommended for proxy deployments:

ALLOWED_HOSTS="yourdomain.com"
USE_X_FORWARDED_HOST=true
CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE=true
SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=true

docs.title: Hook System
docs.text:
Run custom scripts at points of the download lifecycle, configured under HOOKS in config.toml.

Stage Runs pre_run before the main flow starts pre_download once per item, right before that movie/episode starts post_download after each individual download (GUI: once per item) post_run once when the whole execution ends 
# Replace the matching "pre_run = []" / "pre_download = []" / ... line of [HOOKS] with these tables
# (a key can't be declared twice in TOML).
[[HOOKS.pre_run]]
name = "prepare-env"
type = "python"
path = "scripts/prepare.py"
args = ["--clean"]
env = { MY_FLAG = "1" }
cwd = "~"
os = ["linux", "darwin"]
timeout = 60
enabled = true
continue_on_error = true

[[HOOKS.pre_download]]
name = "pre-download-env"
type = "python"
path = "/app/script.py"
args = ["{download_title}"]
timeout = 30

[[HOOKS.post_download]]
name = "post-download-env"
type = "python"
path = "/app/script.py"
args = ["{download_path}"]
env = { MY_FLAG = "1" }
cwd = "~"
os = ["linux"]
timeout = 60

[[HOOKS.post_run]]
name = "notify"
type = "bash"
command = "echo 'Download finished: {download_title}'"
allow_inline_template = true

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Key Description name Label type python, bash, sh, shell, bat, cmd path Script file (alternative to command) command Inline command (alternative to path); args are ignored allow_inline_template true expands {download_title}-style placeholders inside command (off by default: command runs verbatim, while path/args/cwd always expand) args Arguments passed to the script env Extra environment variables cwd Working directory (supports ~ and env vars) os Optional filter: any of "windows", "darwin", "linux" timeout Max seconds (the hook fails if exceeded) enabled Disable without removing continue_on_error false = stop execution when the hook fails

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
• Python: current interpreter.
  • Bash / sh / shell: /bin/bash -c on macOS/Linux.
  • Bat / cmd / shell: cmd /c on Windows.
  • Inline: command instead of path for one-liners.

docs.title: Placeholders
docs.text:
Placeholder Description {download_path} Absolute path of the downloaded file {download_dir} Its directory {download_filename} Its filename {download_id} Internal download id {download_title} Title {download_site} Source site {download_media_type} Media type {download_status} Final status {download_error} Error message, if any {download_success} 1 success, 0 failure {stage} Current hook stage

The same values are exposed as environment variables with an SC_ prefix (SC_DOWNLOAD_PATH, SC_DOWNLOAD_SUCCESS, SC_HOOK_STAGE, ...).

docs.title: CookieInspector
docs.text:
Most services below need data from your logged-in browser session. Open the service's site, log in, click the [CookieInspector] extension (from DISCORD), then use:

Button Reads Used for GET COOKIES Cookies of the current site Crunchyroll, Discovery+, HBO Max, Prime Video, Apple TV GET STORAGE Everything in localStorage Mediaset Infinity, or anything to look up by hand GET TOKEN Only access_token / refresh_token from localStorage Disney+
  • The filter box keeps only keys (or values) containing your text (e.g. st); COPY JSON copies exactly what is shown, on a single line.
  • In login.toml wrap copied JSON in triple single quotes (cookies = '''{"key":"value"}'''): the text stays exactly as copied (backslashes and \n are not interpreted), while plain TOML strings can't hold raw quotes.

Every service section also has args = "": options added to each download of that service (e.g. args = "--quality 1080"). See Default options for a service.

docs.title: Cookie-based services
docs.text:
Open the site, log in, click the extension, GET COOKIES -> COPY JSON, and paste it in Conf/login.toml:

Service Site login.toml section Crunchyroll crunchyroll.com [crunchyroll] Discovery+ [EU] play.discoveryplus.com [discoveryplus] HBO Max play.hbomax.com [hbomax] Amazon Prime Video [EU] primevideo.com [primevideo] Apple TV+ tv.apple.com [appletv] 
[crunchyroll]
cookies = '''<paste_copied_json_here>'''

Discovery+ / HBO Max without the extension: Developer Tools (F12) -> Application -> Cookies, find the st cookie and set st = "<value>" in the [discoveryplus] / [hbomax] section.

docs.title: Mediaset Infinity
docs.text:
1. Open Mediaset and log in (pick your profile).
  2. Extension -> GET STORAGE, type rtilogin_acd in the filter box, Copy JSON.
  3. Add it to Conf/login.toml:
[mediasetinfinity]
rtilogin_acd = '''<paste_copied_value_here>'''

The template ships rtilogin_acd = '''[paste here]''': replace [paste here] with the copied value, or leave it to log in anonymously.

Without the extension: F12 -> Application -> Local Storage -> mediasetinfinity.mediaset.it, copy the rtilogin_acd value.

docs.title: Disney+
docs.text:
1. Open Disney+ and log in.
  2. Extension -> GET TOKEN (shows only access_token and refresh_token) -> Copy JSON.
  3. Add it to Conf/login.toml:
[disney]
token = "<access_token>"
refresh_token = "<refresh_token>"

access_token or token both work for the session token; refresh_token renews it, and renewed values are saved back to the disney section after the first run.

docs.title: Tubi TV: plain credentials
docs.text:
Email/password, no extension. Without them, search returns no results for this site.

[tubi]
email = "your@email.com"
password = "your-password"

docs.title: VibraVid — NAS Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to run VibraVid on a NAS or home server using Docker Compose. Dedicated sections cover Synology Container Manager (DSM 7.2+), QNAP Container Station (ARM64), and generic Linux hosts (Ubuntu, Debian, Raspberry Pi OS, etc.).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker and Docker Compose installed on the NAS
  • The VibraVid repository cloned or downloaded
git clone https://github.com/AstraeLabs/VibraVid.git
cd VibraVid

docs.title: Generic Linux host (Ubuntu, Debian, Raspberry Pi OS, and any distribution)
docs.text: This section applies to any Linux host running Docker: a mini-PC, a Raspberry Pi, a home server, or a machine with an external USB/SATA drive. The steps are the same regardless of distribution.

docs.title: 1. Create your .env file
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env

Edit .env with the paths and settings that match your setup. At minimum, set the download directory and your host IP. For an external drive mounted at /mnt/external:

# Path on the host where downloads will be stored (e.g. an external drive)
VIBRAVID_VIDEO_DIR=/mnt/external/vibravid

# Optional: database and config on the host (recommended for easy backups)
VIBRAVID_DB_DIR=/mnt/data/appdata/vibravid/db
VIBRAVID_CONFIG_DIR=/mnt/data/appdata/vibravid/conf
VIBRAVID_LOGS_DIR=/mnt/data/appdata/vibravid/logs

# Expose on port 8000 (or change to avoid conflicts)
VIBRAVID_PORT=8000

# Allow access from other machines on the LAN
ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost,127.0.0.1,192.168.1.100
CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=http://192.168.1.100:8000

docs.title: 2. Set PUID / PGID (recommended)
docs.text:
To avoid permission issues on the host-mounted folders, set the user and group IDs that own those folders. Run the following on the NAS host to find your user's IDs:

id <your-username>
# Example output: uid=1000(john) gid=1000(john) groups=...

Add to .env:

PUID=1000
PGID=1000

The container entrypoint will remap appuser to these IDs at startup so all downloaded files are owned by your normal user.

docs.title: 3. Start the container
docs.text:
docker compose up -d

On first start, the container automatically: - Seeds /app/Conf from the image defaults if the volume is empty - Runs Django database migrations

Check logs to confirm everything started correctly:

docker compose logs -f

docs.title: 4. Access VibraVid
docs.text:
Open a browser and navigate to:

http://<nas-ip>:8000

docs.title: Step 1 — Open Container Manager
docs.text: In DSM, go to Main Menu → Container Manager.

docs.title: Step 2 — Create a new Project
docs.text:
1. Click Project → Create.
  2. Give the project a name (e.g., vibravid).
  3. Choose Set a path for the project source and select the folder where you cloned the repository (e.g., /volume1/docker/vibravid).
  4. Container Manager will detect docker-compose.yml automatically.

docs.title: Step 3 — Configure environment variables
docs.text:
Before building, click Next to reach the environment variable screen. Add the variables from your .env file here, or set them directly in the UI:

Variable Example value VIBRAVID_VIDEO_DIR /volume2/Media/Movies VIBRAVID_DB_DIR /volume1/docker/vibravid/db VIBRAVID_CONFIG_DIR /volume1/docker/vibravid/conf VIBRAVID_LOGS_DIR /volume1/docker/vibravid/logs PUID 1026 (your DSM user ID) PGID 100 (your DSM group ID) ALLOWED_HOSTS localhost,127.0.0.1,192.168.1.x CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS http://192.168.1.x:8000

To find your Synology user's UID/GID, SSH into the NAS and run:

id <your-dsm-username>

docs.title: Step 4 — Port mapping
docs.text: Container Manager shows the port mapping from docker-compose.yml. The default is 8000 → 8000. Change the left side (host port) if that port is already in use.

docs.title: Step 5 — Build and run
docs.text: Click Done to build the image and start the container. The first build downloads all dependencies and may take a few minutes.

docs.title: Step 6 — Access VibraVid
docs.text: Open http://<nas-ip>:8000 in a browser on your local network.

docs.title: Bind mounts on Synology
docs.text: Bind mounts let you store data in regular Synology shared folders (visible in File Station) instead of Docker-managed volumes.

docs.title: Folder structure example
docs.text:
/volume1/docker/vibravid/
    conf/          ← VIBRAVID_CONFIG_DIR
    db/            ← VIBRAVID_DB_DIR
    logs/          ← VIBRAVID_LOGS_DIR

/volume2/Media/
    Movies/        ← VIBRAVID_VIDEO_DIR (bulk storage)

Create the directories via SSH or File Station before starting the container:

mkdir -p /volume1/docker/vibravid/{conf,db,logs}
mkdir -p /volume2/Media/Movies

Then set the corresponding variables in .env or in the Container Manager UI.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
If downloads land with root ownership, ensure PUID and PGID are set correctly (see Step 3 above). You can verify after the container starts:

ls -ln /volume2/Media/Movies
# Files should show your UID:GID, not 0:0

docs.title: QNAP NAS (ARM64)
docs.text:
QNAP devices frequently use ARM64 processors. The VibraVid Docker image is published as a multi-arch manifest (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64), so you can run it on QNAP without building from source.

Do not run docker compose up --build on ARM64. The source repository includes x86_64-only prebuilt binaries that cause the build to fail on ARM64. Always use docker compose pull to fetch the pre-built image.

docs.title: Setup via QNAP Container Station
docs.text:
1. Install Container Station from the QNAP App Center if not already present.
  2. Open a terminal via SSH or the QNAP shell and clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/AstraeLabs/VibraVid.git
cd VibraVid
  1. Create your .env file:
cp .env.example .env

Edit .env for your QNAP paths. QNAP shared folders are typically under /share/:

VIBRAVID_VIDEO_DIR=/share/Multimedia/vibravid
VIBRAVID_DB_DIR=/share/Container/vibravid/db
VIBRAVID_CONFIG_DIR=/share/Container/vibravid/conf
VIBRAVID_LOGS_DIR=/share/Container/vibravid/logs
VIBRAVID_PORT=8000
ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost,127.0.0.1,<qnap-ip>
CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=http://<qnap-ip>:8000
  1. Find your user's UID/GID:
id <your-username>

Add to .env:

PUID=<your-uid>
PGID=<your-gid>
  1. Pull the pre-built ARM64 image and start:
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

Docker automatically selects the ARM64 image variant from the multi-arch manifest.

  1. Access VibraVid at http://<qnap-ip>:8000.

docs.title: Manual update
docs.text:
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

This pulls the latest published image and recreates the container without touching volumes.

docs.title: In-app update (if enabled)
docs.text: When a new version is available, VibraVid will show an update banner in the web UI. Follow the on-screen instructions to apply the update.

docs.title: "DisallowedHost" or "403 Forbidden"
docs.text:
Your NAS IP is not in ALLOWED_HOSTS. Add it:

ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost,127.0.0.1,192.168.1.100
CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=http://192.168.1.100:8000

Then recreate the container:

docker compose up -d --force-recreate

docs.title: Downloads owned by root
docs.text: PUID / PGID are not set or do not match the folder owner. Check with id <user> on the NAS host and set the variables accordingly.

docs.title: Port already in use
docs.text: Change VIBRAVID_PORT to a free port (e.g., 8080), update CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS to match, and recreate the container.

docs.title: Container exits immediately
docs.text:
Check logs for Python errors:

docker compose logs --tail=50

Common causes: invalid config.toml (delete the conf volume and let the entrypoint re-seed it), missing bind-mount directory (create it on the host first), or a stale database migration (run docker compose down -v and start fresh).

docs.title: Remote server (resolve on a server, download on a client)
docs.text:
One machine runs the services (login, search, title/track/manifest resolution); any number of clients run the download.

Where What runs Server service code: login, search, seasons/episodes, manifest and playback resolution, the service's own license call Client track selection (-sv/-sa/-ss), download, decrypt, mux, naming/output folders, vault lookup, your own CDM

Licenses, per API key:

  • Client CDM (default): your CDM builds the challenge; the server relays it to the service (using the service's signed call if it has one). Lookup order: manifest -> KID -> vault -> CDM only if the key isn't in the vault.
  • Server CDM (server_cdm): the server runs the whole key flow (vault, then its CDM) and returns kid:key pairs; the client needs no CDM. Granted per key.

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
Conf/remote.json:

{
  "serve": {
    "host": "127.0.0.1",
    "port": 8786,
    "sites": ["appletv", "disney"],
    "users": {
      "a-long-random-secret": { "username": "alice", "sites": ["appletv"], "server_cdm": true },
      "another-secret":       { "username": "bob" }
    }
  }
}
Key Description users API key -> username, optional sites allowlist, optional server_cdm (default false) sites Optional global allowlist; a key gets the intersection with its own list. Omit a list for "everything" host Default 127.0.0.1; change only to really expose the server session_ttl Idle seconds (default 300) max_sessions Default 100 bind_session_to_ip Default true 
python GUI/manage.py remote_serve        # --host / --port override the config

It refuses to start without a key; --no-key serves without keys, loopback only.

The server never uses an account of its own: each request runs with the client's login (see Logging in through the server). A service with no client login runs anonymous.

docs.title: Client
docs.text:
Add the server to your Conf/remote.json:

{
  "remote_services": {
    "home": { "url": "http://203.0.113.10:8786", "api_key": "a-long-random-secret", "server_cdm": false }
  }
}

python manual.py --server home -i appletv -s "Some Title" -S 1 -E "*"
python manual.py --server -i appletv -s "Some Film" --item 0          # only one server configured
python manual.py --server home -i appletv -s "Some Show" -S 1 -E 3 --server-opt drm=playready --server-opt atmos=true
  • --server [NAME]: NAME can be omitted when exactly one server is configured.
  • -i takes the site name (the index works only if the service is installed locally).
  • -s, --item (0-based), -S, -E work as in a normal run; otherwise you are prompted (row number, q to quit).
  • Service options are flags (--url, --store, ...) or --server-opt KEY=VALUE (repeatable); options set for a locally installed service are forwarded too.
  • server_cdm: true applies only if the API key has the grant; otherwise your local CDM is used with a warning.

docs.title: Writing a service for a remote server
docs.text:
A service works unchanged if it reads its login when needed (config_manager.login.get(...)) and keeps its logged-in client in a module global named like _client, _xxx_client, _client_by_region...

  • Don't read the login at import time (_token = config_manager.login.get(...) at module level): it would be read once, for nobody. Read it inside the login function. (disney still does this.)
  • To name identity-bound globals yourself, add _identity_state = ("_client", "_session") to the service module; it replaces the naming guess.

docs.title: Logging in through the server (--login, --logout)
docs.text:
A service's own login runs on the server while the account stays with you:

python manual.py --server home -i <service> --login
python manual.py --server home -i <service> --logout
  • Output (pairing link and code, progress) appears in your terminal; links are not opened on the server.
  • Its questions (region, "press Enter after authorizing"...) are asked in your terminal.
  • Tokens are stored in your Conf/login.toml / .cache; the server writes nothing and forgets the login at the end (Ctrl+C cancels; an unanswered login ends after 5 minutes).
  • The service doesn't need to be installed on the client.

Outside a login, a service that stops to ask something fails at once (asked for input a server cannot give). Options like --csv (reads a local file) must run locally.

docs.title: Service options (--url and the rest)
docs.text:
The server lists each service's own options (--url, --store, --atmos, --drm...) at GET /api/remote/sites/<site>/info/, so they work without the service installed locally:

python manual.py --server home -i appletv --url "https://tv.apple.com/it/movie/..." --store US
python manual.py --server home -i appletv -s "Some Title" --atmos

--url replaces -s (the server resolves the link without searching). The same values go to search, seasons and download. --server-opt KEY=VALUE sets any option by hand.

docs.title: Exposing the server
docs.text:
The server has no TLS. Pick one:

  • a VPN (Tailscale, WireGuard), binding to the VPN address: simplest and safest;
  • a reverse proxy with HTTPS (Caddy, nginx) or a tunnel in front of 127.0.0.1:8786;
  • a LAN address with --host.

Sessions are bound to the client IP (REMOTE_ADDR); behind a reverse proxy that is the proxy's address, shared by everyone. Set bind_session_to_ip to false if that gets in the way (the API key is still required).

Anyone with a key can use the server's accounts: one key per person, plus the sites allowlist. Keys are compared in constant time and never logged (only the username).

docs.title: TGBot — Telegram "trigger-download" bot
docs.text:
Triggers VibraVid downloads from Telegram chat. It never sends files: it searches, starts the download and reports status as text (queued -> downloading NN% -> completed, with the saved path). The file stays on the VibraVid machine; fetch it with SMB, Syncthing, SFTP, etc.

It uses Telethon (MTProto), already used elsewhere, so you need api_id / api_hash (free at https://my.telegram.org) besides the BotFather bot_token.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Credentials (bot_token, api_id, api_hash, allowed_users) come only from TG_* environment variables, typically a dedicated .env.telegram (copy .env.telegram.example) loaded by the telegram service in docker-compose.yml. No fallback to login.toml/config.toml; changing them needs a container restart.

Non-sensitive settings live in [TELEGRAM] of Conf/config.toml (hot-reloaded), falling back to the TG_* variables:

[TELEGRAM]
enabled = false
gui_url = "http://vibravid:8000"
max_results = 8
Variable Required Description TG_BOT_TOKEN yes Token from BotFather TG_API_ID / TG_API_HASH yes From https://my.telegram.org TG_ALLOWED_USERS recommended Comma-separated numeric Telegram IDs allowed to use the bot; empty = everyone TG_GUI_URL no Internal GUI URL (default http://vibravid:8000) VIBRAVID_BOT_SECRET no Shared secret authenticating the bot to the GUI (X-VibraVid-Token); must also be set on the GUI side

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Description /scarica <title> Search the configured sites (respecting /sito) and show results as buttons. Movies/songs/albums start at once; series ask for a season, then an episode or the whole season. Without arguments: asks title, then site /sito (/siti, /filtro) Choose what /scarica searches: "🌐 All sites" (default), a category (Movies/Series/Anime/Music) or one site. Saved per user; a "🔍 Repeat" button reruns the last search with the new filter /coda (/downloads) Active downloads (with %) and queued ones /annulla Your in-progress downloads as buttons to cancel /stato (/status) Free/total disk space and active/max download slots /log Latest search/download log lines. Variants: /log 100 (line count), /log err (errors/warnings), /log bot (the bot's in-memory log, cleared on restart)

While downloading, the message updates with the percentage and a "❌ Cancel download" button; it ends with "✅ completed" (and the path) or a summary of failures / already-in-library items.

docs.title: Bridge to the GUI
docs.text: The bot calls the GUI over HTTP (gui_url) using the api/bot/* endpoints plus /api/get-downloads/ for /coda. With VIBRAVID_BOT_SECRET set, every request carries X-VibraVid-Token; without it the endpoints are unauthenticated, so set it before exposing the GUI beyond your LAN.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text: Dedicated container (telegram in docker-compose.yml): same image as vibravid, entrypoint docker/telegram-entrypoint.sh, which runs python docker/telegram_bot/bot.py as a script (not -m: imports are absolute, see PYTHONPATH=/app in the Dockerfile).

docs.title: TUI (Terminal User Interface)
docs.text: Terminal interface built with Textual; no browser needed.

docs.title: Launch
docs.text: python tui.py          # or: uv run python tui.py  /  python manual.py --tui

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Every screen has the same frame: a top bar the content, and at the bottom the shortcuts of the current screen above the navigation bar ([H] Home, [d] Downloads, [ESC] Back, [Ctrl+Q] Quit...).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Global search deduplication: one result per title across all providers, showing every source.
  • Multi-provider detail: [Providers] -> [Seasons] -> [Episodes] columns; switch provider without going back to search.
  • i18n (IT / EN): detected from the OS language, across all screens.
  • Queue & batch manager: add, remove, reorder and retry jobs with custom CLI arguments and tags.
  • Live progress: progress, speed, segment counts, track details; open folder / launch file when done.
  • System & DRM inspector: external binaries (ffmpeg, flux, mkvmerge, ...), CDM device status, log viewer, and a Refresh external import button (applies the newest commit of the imp_service repositories at once) and an Updates tab (version info, release check cached 24 h, skipped with auto_check_update = false, Download update for binary builds: downloads the matching executable with SHA-256 verification without replacing the running one).

docs.title: Cover art
docs.text:
Search and detail show the cover of the highlighted title: the film or series poster, the season poster or the episode still from TMDB (then IMDb/TVDB, see metadata_provider), the service's own image as a last resort, and for songs and albums the cover the service returned (Amazon Music, YouTube Music...). Images are cached in .cache/covers.

How it is drawn follows tui_images (DEFAULT):

Value Result auto A real, scaled image if the terminal supports the Kitty or Sixel protocol and textual-image is installed, otherwise characters sixel / kitty Force that protocol blocks Half-block characters (two pixels per cell): works in any truecolor terminal but is coarse off No covers

Real images work in Windows Terminal 1.22+, WezTerm, kitty and iTerm2, and in VS Code with terminal.integrated.enableImages turned on. They do not work in the legacy Windows console, GNOME Terminal or Warp, and inside tmux only with Sixel enabled. If the cover shows up black or garbled, set tui_images = "blocks".

docs.title: Adding a DRM Key Vault
docs.text:
A vault is an external DRM key store that VibraVid queries before falling back to CDM extraction. Most vaults need only a config entry under DRM.vault. See Configuration → Multiple / self-hosted DRM vaults for the fields.

[DRM.vault.default]
url = "https://drm-db.dev"
token = ""

[DRM.vault.myvault]
url = "https://drm.example.com"
token = "..."
protocol = "custom"

[DRM.vault.public]
url = "https://vault.example.org"
token = "..."

protocol is optional: without it VibraVid detects it once and caches it in .cache/services/vault/universal_<name>.json.

docs.title: A new protocol
docs.text:
Only a backend that speaks none of custom / api / json / query needs code. Subclass BaseVault (VibraVid/utils/vault/base.py) and override what the backend supports:

from VibraVid.utils.vault.base import BaseVault

class MyVault(BaseVault):
    @property
    def is_connected(self) -> bool:
        return True

    def get_keys_by_kids(self, license_url, kids, pssh=None) -> list[str]:
        return []  # ["kid:key", ...]
  • get_keys_by_kids() is the lookup DRMManager uses.
  • is_writable + set_keys(): only if the vault should receive newly extracted keys (default: read-only).
  • report_wrong_key(): only if the backend can record a key proven wrong by flux's key-sanity check.
  • replace_key(): swaps a reported key for the corrected one (the default just calls set_keys()).

Then return your instance for its config key in DRMManager._build_vaults() (VibraVid/core/drm/manager.py).
